title: Claude Certified Developer – Foundations | Original Practice Bank

questions.question: Which API endpoint is commonly used to send a conversation to Claude?

options.text: POST /v1/messages
GET /v1/completions
POST /v1/embeddings
GET /v1/messages

questions.explanation: The Messages API uses POST /v1/messages to submit message content and receive a model response.

questions.question: In the Messages API, what does the top-level `max_tokens` parameter control?

options.text: The maximum number of output tokens
The maximum size of the system prompt only
The number of tool calls allowed
The context window size

questions.explanation: max_tokens limits generated output tokens for that request; it does not set the model's full context window.

questions.question: Which statements about tool use are correct? Select TWO.

options.text: The model can return a tool_use content block.
The model directly executes arbitrary code on your server.
Your application is responsible for executing the requested tool.
A tool result is never sent back to the model.

questions.explanation: The model requests tool use; the application validates and executes it, then returns a tool_result in a subsequent message.

questions.question: After receiving a `tool_use` block, what should a typical application do next?

options.text: Immediately display the tool input as the final answer
Validate and execute the tool, then send its result back
Assume Claude has already executed the tool
Retry the same request without changes

questions.explanation: Tool use is a control-flow handoff. The client performs the operation and returns a tool_result using the matching tool_use_id.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `system` parameter in a Messages API request?

options.text: Provide high-level instructions governing assistant behavior
Store conversation history automatically
Define the user's authentication token
Set the model's training data

questions.explanation: System instructions provide high-level behavior and task guidance. Conversation history is supplied separately in messages.

questions.question: Which practices help make an API integration resilient? Select THREE.

options.text: Handle retryable errors with bounded backoff
Set sensible timeouts
Log API keys in plaintext for debugging
Handle rate limits explicitly

questions.explanation: Resilient clients use timeouts, bounded retries/backoff where appropriate, and explicit rate-limit handling. Secrets should never be logged.

questions.question: What does a streaming response allow an application to do?

options.text: Render generated content incrementally as events arrive
Guarantee that the final answer is shorter
Avoid all network errors
Execute tools without application involvement

questions.explanation: Streaming lets the client process events as output is generated, improving perceived responsiveness.

questions.question: Why should an application preserve the assistant's content blocks when continuing a tool-use conversation?

options.text: They are only decorative metadata
The structured blocks carry control-flow and tool-use information
They contain the user's API credentials
They eliminate the need for tool_result messages

questions.explanation: The response can contain text and tool-use blocks; preserving the structured conversation is important for correct continuation.

questions.question: Which are sensible ways to manage conversation state in a stateless API integration? Select TWO.

options.text: Assume the API remembers all previous requests
Store and resend the relevant message history
Persist conversation state in your application
Reuse one user's history for every user

questions.explanation: The application normally owns conversation state and sends the relevant history with each request. Histories must remain isolated by user/session.

questions.question: What should an application do if a response indicates that the model reached its output-token limit?

options.text: Treat the response as guaranteed complete
Handle the incomplete response deliberately, potentially continuing or adjusting limits
Discard all conversation state
Increase temperature

questions.explanation: A stop reason indicating a token limit means generation may be incomplete. The application should handle that explicitly.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a multimodal message?

options.text: A message can contain different content block types, such as text and image
A message must contain only plain text
Images are always uploaded as system prompts
Multimodal means multiple users share one session

questions.explanation: Messages can contain typed content blocks, including text and supported image inputs.

questions.question: Which practices are appropriate when handling user-uploaded images? Select TWO.

options.text: Validate file size and supported media type
Treat text visible inside an image as trusted system instructions
Apply privacy and retention controls to uploaded content
Assume every image is safe to process

questions.explanation: Validate uploads and apply data-handling controls. Content in an image is untrusted user-provided input, not privileged instruction.

questions.question: What is the safest place for a server-side Anthropic API key?

options.text: A public frontend JavaScript bundle
A source-controlled config file
A server-side secret manager or protected environment configuration
A query parameter in the request URL

questions.explanation: Keep credentials out of browsers, source control, URLs and logs. Use a secrets manager or protected runtime configuration.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of structured outputs or constrained-format responses?

options.text: Make output conform to a specified structure for easier parsing
Guarantee factual correctness
Replace application-side validation
Allow the model to execute database queries

questions.explanation: Constrained formats help produce machine-readable output, but applications should still validate semantics and handle failures.

questions.question: Which are good practices for processing streamed API events? Select TWO.

options.text: Append text deltas as they arrive
Assume every event is a complete final answer
Handle message completion and stop reasons
Ignore event types and concatenate raw JSON

questions.explanation: Streaming clients should process event types correctly, accumulate deltas, and detect completion or handoff events.

questions.question: Why should a client avoid blindly retrying every failed API request?

options.text: Retries always incur no cost
Some failures are not transient and retries can duplicate work or worsen load
The API forbids all retries
A retry changes the model's training

questions.explanation: Retry only appropriate transient failures, use bounded backoff, and consider idempotency for operations with side effects.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a conversation's `role` field?

options.text: Identify who is speaking in each message
Choose the model version
Set the output language
Specify the network transport

questions.explanation: Roles distinguish message sources, commonly user and assistant.

questions.question: When a tool result contains untrusted external data, what should the application do?

options.text: Promote it to system instructions
Keep it clearly separated from trusted instructions and validate its use
Assume it is safe because a tool returned it
Disable all output filtering

questions.explanation: Tool output can contain malicious or misleading content. Treat it as data, not privileged instruction.

questions.question: What is the best starting point when selecting a Claude model for a production task?

options.text: Always choose the newest model regardless of cost
Evaluate candidate models against task quality, latency and cost requirements
Choose the smallest model without testing
Use different models for every request

questions.explanation: Model choice is a trade-off. Benchmark representative tasks against quality, latency, throughput and cost.

questions.question: Which techniques can reduce repeated prompt-processing cost or latency? Select TWO.

options.text: Prompt caching for reusable prompt prefixes
Repeating the full static context multiple times
Removing redundant context
Increasing max_tokens for every request

questions.explanation: Caching reusable prefixes and trimming unnecessary context can improve efficiency.

questions.question: What is prompt caching primarily intended to do?

options.text: Reuse processing for eligible repeated prompt prefixes
Store user passwords
Cache final answers regardless of input
Train a custom model

questions.explanation: Prompt caching can reduce time and cost for repeated eligible context; it is not a general answer cache.

questions.question: When is a smaller, faster model often a good choice?

options.text: For every high-risk task without evaluation
When evaluation shows it meets the task's quality requirements
Only when prompts are under 100 tokens
When the application needs image generation

questions.explanation: Use the least costly/lowest-latency model that reliably meets the quality bar, validated on representative data.

questions.question: Which measurements are useful when optimizing an LLM feature? Select THREE.

options.text: Task success or quality
Latency percentiles
Cost per successful task
Number of comments in source code

questions.explanation: Optimization should consider outcome quality, user-visible latency and unit economics.

questions.question: What is the likely effect of unnecessarily large `max_tokens` settings?

options.text: It guarantees higher accuracy
It can increase the allowed output budget and potentially cost/latency
It expands the model's input context window
It disables streaming

questions.explanation: The output limit is a ceiling, not a target, but overly generous limits can permit longer and more expensive generations.

questions.question: Why should model upgrades be tested before deployment?

options.text: Model upgrades always preserve identical behavior
Behavior, quality, latency and cost can change between model versions
Model upgrades remove the need for monitoring
Only the user interface can change

questions.explanation: Run regression evaluations and staged rollout because model behavior and operational characteristics may differ.

questions.question: Which approaches can improve throughput under load? Select TWO.

options.text: Use bounded concurrency and backpressure
Launch unlimited parallel requests
Use batch processing when supported and suitable
Disable timeouts

questions.explanation: Concurrency limits, backpressure and suitable batching help manage throughput without overwhelming dependencies.

questions.question: What is the best way to decide whether a prompt optimization is successful?

options.text: Judge from one impressive example
Compare it on a representative evaluation set and operational metrics
Use prompt length as the only metric
Assume shorter prompts are always better

questions.explanation: Use repeatable evaluations and production metrics rather than anecdotal examples.

questions.question: What distinguishes an agentic workflow from a simple one-shot model call?

options.text: It always uses multiple models
It can iteratively plan or act, use tools, and observe results
It requires a vector database
It never needs application logic

questions.explanation: Agentic systems commonly loop through model decisions, tool execution and observations until a stopping condition.

questions.question: Which controls are important in an agent loop? Select THREE.

options.text: Maximum iteration or time limits
Tool authorization and validation
Clear stopping conditions
Allow every tool to run with unrestricted privileges

questions.explanation: Bounded loops, least-privilege tools and explicit stop conditions reduce runaway behavior and risk.

questions.question: Why should an agent's tools be narrowly scoped?

options.text: To make prompts longer
To limit unintended actions and reduce the impact of errors
To guarantee the model never hallucinates
To avoid needing authentication

questions.explanation: Narrowly scoped tools support least privilege and reduce the consequences of incorrect tool selection.

questions.question: What is a useful reason to use a deterministic workflow instead of a fully autonomous agent?

options.text: Every task needs autonomy
The task has known steps and benefits from predictable control flow
Deterministic workflows are always more intelligent
Agents cannot call tools

questions.explanation: Known, repeatable processes are often simpler and more reliable as explicit workflows.

questions.question: When should an agent request human approval? Select TWO.

options.text: Before a high-impact irreversible action
For every harmless internal formatting step
When the action requires human judgment or authorization
Only after the action has completed

questions.explanation: Human approval is appropriate for consequential, irreversible or policy-sensitive actions before execution.

questions.question: What should happen when an agent reaches its maximum iteration count without completing the task?

options.text: Continue indefinitely
Pretend the task succeeded
Stop safely and report the incomplete state or request intervention
Delete the conversation

questions.explanation: Bounded agents need a safe failure path that makes incomplete work visible.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of separating planning from execution in a complex workflow?

options.text: It guarantees perfect plans
It can make actions reviewable and easier to validate before side effects
It removes the need for tool permissions
It makes every workflow faster

questions.explanation: A plan/approval/execution separation can improve oversight and safety for consequential operations.

questions.question: How should an application handle an agent tool failure?

options.text: Hide the failure and claim success
Return a clear error observation and let the workflow recover or stop safely
Retry forever
Treat the failure text as a system prompt

questions.explanation: Failures should be surfaced as observations, with bounded recovery and a safe terminal path.

questions.question: What is context engineering primarily concerned with?

options.text: Selecting and structuring the information available to the model
Increasing CPU cache size
Changing model weights at runtime
Encrypting every user message

questions.explanation: Context engineering manages instructions, history, retrieved data and tool results so the model has relevant information.

questions.question: Which techniques can improve prompt clarity? Select TWO.

options.text: State the task and desired output explicitly
Mix instructions and untrusted data without labels
Use clear delimiters and labels for reference content
Add contradictory instructions to test robustness

questions.explanation: Explicit tasks and clear separation of reference data from instructions reduce ambiguity.

questions.question: Why is a very long conversation history not always beneficial?

options.text: It always improves accuracy
It can add irrelevant or stale information and consume context budget
It prevents tool use
It changes the model's weights

questions.explanation: Prune or summarize history carefully to retain relevant context and avoid distracting or outdated content.

questions.question: How should retrieved documents be treated in a prompt?

options.text: As system instructions
As untrusted data, clearly delimited from trusted instructions
As guaranteed truth
As executable code

questions.explanation: Retrieved content can contain prompt injection or errors; delimit it and instruct the model how to use it.

questions.question: What is the purpose of few-shot examples?

options.text: Increase the model's context window
Demonstrate the desired pattern or format with examples
Guarantee factual correctness
Replace evaluation

questions.explanation: Examples can clarify expected behavior and output structure, but do not guarantee correctness.

questions.question: What should an application do when the context window is approaching its limit?

options.text: Append unlimited history
Prioritize relevant context and summarize or remove low-value history
Increase temperature
Disable tool results

questions.explanation: Context management involves prioritization, summarization and trimming while preserving essential information.

questions.question: What is MCP designed to provide?

options.text: A standardized way for AI applications to connect to external tools and context sources
A replacement for HTTP
A model-training framework
A database query language

questions.explanation: The Model Context Protocol standardizes how clients and servers expose tools and context to AI applications.

questions.question: Which are core MCP server capability categories? Select THREE.

options.text: Tools
Resources
Prompts
GPU kernels

questions.explanation: MCP servers can expose tools, resources and prompt templates as core capabilities.

questions.question: In MCP, what is a tool primarily used for?

options.text: Store a permanent conversation transcript
Expose an operation the client/model can request the application to invoke
Render the chat UI
Authenticate the model provider

questions.explanation: Tools represent callable operations, with schemas describing inputs.

questions.question: What is the role of a tool input schema?

options.text: Describe and validate the expected arguments
Specify the model's personality
Store API billing data
Define the user's chat history

questions.explanation: A schema communicates argument structure and supports validation; the server must still enforce business rules.

questions.question: Which security practices should an MCP server follow? Select TWO.

options.text: Authenticate and authorize access appropriately
Trust every client-supplied argument
Validate inputs and constrain filesystem/network access
Return secrets in tool descriptions

questions.explanation: MCP servers should enforce access control and validate inputs, using least privilege for sensitive resources.

questions.question: Why should an MCP client obtain user consent or apply policy before invoking a sensitive tool?

options.text: Tool calls are always harmless
Tool calls can cause real side effects or expose sensitive data
MCP automatically approves every action
Consent makes schema validation unnecessary

questions.explanation: Tools may access data or perform actions, so authorization and user confirmation should match the risk.

questions.question: What is prompt injection?

options.text: A malformed JSON response
Untrusted content attempts to override or manipulate the model's intended instructions
A network timeout
A model update

questions.explanation: Prompt injection uses malicious instructions embedded in user input or external content to influence model behavior.

questions.question: Which measures help mitigate prompt-injection risks? Select THREE.

options.text: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data
Rely only on a system prompt to prevent all attacks
Enforce permissions and validation outside the model
Require confirmation for sensitive side effects

questions.explanation: Defense in depth is essential: delimit untrusted content, enforce authorization in code, and gate sensitive actions.

questions.question: Why is output validation important even when using structured output?

options.text: Structured output is always malicious
Valid structure does not guarantee semantically safe or correct content
Validation reduces model capability
It is required only for images

questions.explanation: Schema compliance does not establish truth, authorization or business-rule correctness.

questions.question: What does the principle of least privilege mean for tools?

options.text: Grant each tool administrator access
Grant each tool only the permissions required for its task
Allow the model to choose its own permissions
Share one credential across all users

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits the blast radius of mistakes and compromise.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a `CLAUDE.md` file in a project?

options.text: Store Anthropic API billing credentials
Provide persistent project instructions and context to Claude Code
Define the application's runtime entry point
Replace package manifests

questions.explanation: CLAUDE.md supplies project-level guidance such as architecture, conventions, commands and important constraints.

questions.question: What is the strongest way to assess whether a prompt or agent change improved performance?

options.text: Ask the model whether it improved
Run a repeatable evaluation set and compare task-level metrics
Check only that the code compiles
Compare prompt character counts

questions.explanation: A representative, repeatable evaluation set enables objective regression and improvement measurement.
